elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Retained 13.5 still provides that Developments "shall be owned by Corio, unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights", and the closing sentence leaves ownership of Software enhancements developed solely by Corio or jointly "to be negotiated by the parties". The redline does not reverse either carve-out, so Corio does not own all work product created for it.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: The existing assignment ("Commerce One hereby assigns all rights in and to such Developments to Corio") is expressly limited to "such Developments" and is contradicted by the retained sentence giving Commerce One "all ownership rights" in supported Developments; no assignment covers that category or the to-be-negotiated enhancements.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Opening words retained unchanged: "Subject to Commerce One's pre-existing ownership of any materials or technology provided to Corio".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The inserted grant is limited to Developments/enhancements "Commerce One owns or retains ownership of"; nothing grants Corio a perpetual licence to Commerce One pre-existing materials or technology embedded in Developments, which remain carved out by the opening "Subject to" language.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Same defect: the "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license" attaches only to Commerce One-owned Developments, not to embedded Commerce One pre-existing IP.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No royalty-free grant reaches Commerce One's pre-existing materials or technology embedded in the Developments; the new sentence covers only owned Developments/enhancements.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The redline adds only a limit on any licence granted to Commerce One in Corio/Customer data; no affirmative sentence states that Corio retains all right, title and interest in that data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Any license granted to Commerce One in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Corio or its Customers is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement." The trigger covers every category of Corio data (belonging to, supplied by, processed for), not selected data types.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The retained final sentence expressly contemplates enhancements "developed jointly by the parties" with ownership left to future negotiation; no express no-joint-ownership statement was added.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Existing, unamended language preserves Commerce One's position: "Subject to Commerce One's pre-existing ownership of any materials or technology provided to Corio" (and Software ownership elsewhere).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Commerce One grants Corio a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license..." applying "[t]o the extent Commerce One owns or retains ownership of any Developments, enhancements, modifications or derivative works developed by Corio under this Section 13" — i.e. exactly the categories Corio would otherwise hold no rights in.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license" in the inserted grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" appears expressly in the inserted licence grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free" appears expressly in the inserted licence grant.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense the same for Corio's business."

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "use, modify and sublicense the same for Corio's business" — sublicensing right is express and scoped to Corio's business.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Second inserted sentence confines any Commerce One licence in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Corio or its Customers to "processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement"; no distribution, resale or broader "purposes contemplated" wording is granted.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the inserted grant supplies all four licence qualifiers (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free) plus use, modify and sublicense for Corio's business, over precisely the Developments/enhancements Commerce One owns or retains — the gap the finding identifies. Vendor's generic tools/know-how ownership survives via the retained "pre-existing ownership" carve-out, and the added data sentence satisfies the Customer Data limit.

Preferred level is not reached and should not be claimed: ownership still flips to Commerce One for Developments it supports on an ongoing basis, Software enhancements remain subject to future negotiation, joint development is still contemplated with no no-joint-ownership sentence, no affirmative statement that Corio retains all rights in its data, and no licence reaches Commerce One pre-existing IP embedded in Developments. To move to preferred, the drafter would need to delete the "unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One..." carve-out, replace the closing negotiation sentence with Corio ownership plus assignment, add a Corio data-ownership sentence, and add an express no-joint-ownership statement.

Minimality holds: two concise insertions, no deletions, no paraphrase of retained words, no survival tails, expense language, procedures or extra remedies; every added term maps to a fallback element.

Intent preserved: the grant is expressly conditional ("To the extent Commerce One owns or retains ownership"), so it does not contradict the retained ownership allocation, the assignment sentence, the Employee NDA/Invention Agreement covenants, or the pre-existing-materials carve-out; no dangling cross-references are created.

Minor drafting note only (not a failure): the new sentence uses lowercase "the services under this Agreement" while the contract defines "Corio Services"; tightening to the defined term would remove any argument that the limit is anchored to an undefined concept.
